flags.title: Asks you to pay before you start
flags.why: Real employers never ask you to buy equipment, training or software up front, even with a promise of reimbursement.
flags.evidence: Once hired, purchase your home-office kit ($450) through our approved vendor and you'll be reimbursed with your first check.

flags.title: Sender email does not match the company
flags.why: The message claims to be from Amazon but was sent from a free gmail.com address. Big companies email from their own domain.

flags.title: Link goes to a lookalike domain
flags.why: The link's domain looks like Amazon but isn't one of its official domains.

flags.title: Reported as a scam by other job seekers
flags.why: Other HireGuard users reported this sender or website as a scam.

flags.title: Interview only over a chat app
flags.why: Scammers avoid phone or video calls so they can't be identified. Real recruiters schedule calls or video interviews.
flags.evidence: Interviews are conducted on Telegram - add @amzn_hr_team.

flags.title: Pay that's too good for the work
flags.why: Very high pay for simple, no-experience work is a common lure.
flags.evidence: Your resume was selected for a Remote Data Entry Associate role at Amazon ($42/hr).

flags.title: Domain was registered very recently
flags.why: Scam sites are often created days before the messages go out. Real companies' domains are usually years old.

flags.title: Pressure to respond fast
flags.why: Urgency is used to stop you from checking the offer before you act.
flags.evidence: Please respond within 2 hours to keep your spot.

flags.title: Several warning signs together
flags.why: One sign alone can be innocent. Several different ones in the same message is a strong scam pattern.
flags.evidence: 8 different warning signs in this message
